checksum.scope: No application-layer checksum is documented; CAN's own CRC covers the frame. Whether state-changing frames carry a counter or authentication is an open question -- Bosch's tamper detection implies integrity checking somewhere.

messages.advanced_reason: Transmits onto a live bus that has a motor on it, and is unconfirmed -- one source, not reproduced. Bosch detects and records tampering, and a flagged unit can be refused service and lose warranty, a consequence that outlives the change that caused it. Reproduce passively first, wheel off the ground, and know your recovery path before sending anything.
messages.description: Reported start/stop command -- the entire published message catalogue for this system. Sent as: cansend can0 061#00
messages.name: start_stop
messages.notes: Reproducing or refuting this frame is the natural first milestone after a clean passive capture.

bus.notes: Bring the interface up with: ip link set can0 type can bitrate 500000. Tooling: can-utils (candump/cansend), python-can for live viewing, cannelloni for UDP-over-CAN to a workstation, or SuperCAN firmware on an Adafruit Feather M4 CAN Express. Kiox display internals, for anyone working on the display itself: STM32F469IIH6 CPU, W25M512JV 512 Mbit SPI flash, W9864G6KH 64 Mbit SDRAM.

device.name: Bosch Performance Line CX (Gen4)
device.notes:
The most closed mainstream e-bike system, and the one that most often stops an independent repair. Fault detail, component pairing and firmware updates are gated behind Bosch dealer tooling and the eBike Connect app, so a workshop without dealer access can see THAT a bike has faulted without being able to say why, and cannot re-pair a replaced motor, battery or display. (The eBike Flow app is for the smart system / BES3 only; Gen4/BES2 pairs through eBike Connect.)
THIS SPEC IS A STARTING KIT, NOT A PROTOCOL. What is documented below is how to get onto the bus -- bitrate, breakout pinout, tooling. The public message catalogue is a SINGLE frame. There is no decoded field mapping for speed, assist level, battery state or error codes yet; building one is the work.
NO RADIO ON THE BUS, NO SOCKET: unlike every other vehicle target here, there is nothing to scan for at the system level. Reaching the bus needs a CAN interface and physical access to the harness. Budget for hardware, not an afternoon with a phone. One caveat on the wording: a Kiox (BUI350) display DOES advertise BLE -- it pairs with the eBike Connect app and with BLE heart-rate straps -- but that link belongs to the display and is not a path onto the bus. That display link is now documented below (see `services:`) from static analysis of the eBike Connect app: two proprietary GATT services (MCSP for CoAP data, BSS for security), a fragmented message transport with CRC-16, certificate-based DH key establishment and ChaCha20-Poly1305 message protection. It is the richest documented surface on this system -- but it terminates at the display, and pairing is gated by a per-device key issued by the Bosch backend, so it changes nothing about reaching the bus itself.
NO CAN IN THE APP: the eBike Connect app contains zero CAN code -- no SocketCAN, no CAN-frame handling anywhere in its code; it talks BLE (and backend REST) only. The CAN open questions in this spec are therefore NOT resolved by app analysis and stay open.
VERIFICATION: link parameters and wiring are `reported` and reproducible. The single frame below is `hypothesis` -- reported by one source and not reproduced by us. Nothing here has been observed on our own bus. Everything under `services:` is app-confirmed, not hardware-tested: it comes from static analysis of the eBike Connect app, and no frame of the Kiox BLE link has been captured or replayed by us.
METHOD: passive capture first, always. This is a bus with a motor on it. Capture a full session (power-on, each assist level, walk mode, an induced fault on a stand), diff single-variable changes to isolate candidate IDs, and identify which node emits which ID by capturing with components disconnected one at a time. Only then consider transmitting.
SINCE THIS SPEC WAS WRITTEN (2026-05): Bosch published an official, free "Live Data Interface" BLE GATT specification (V1.0, 2026-05-01) -- 13 read-only live data points (speed, SoC, rider power, cadence, odometer, lock/light/charger state) with permissive terms. It covers the smart system (BES3) only and does not unlock Gen4/BES2, but it is Bosch's first open protocol and a policy U-turn worth recording.

credentials.notes: No WiFi, no account and no passphrase for the bus: physical access to the harness is the only credential. The Kiox BLE link is the opposite: pairing requires a per-device encryptedPreSharedKey provisioned from the Bosch backend and stored on the device record (app-confirmed: it is a field on the app's shared device model, the app refuses to connect without it, and the key material is parsed as a "backend pre-shared key"). No backend-issued key, no link -- third-party pairing is backend-gated, not hardware-tested.

factory_reset.effect: No user- or workshop-accessible factory reset. Component pairing and any reset-like operation run through Bosch dealer tooling. Recording that gap honestly is the point of this entry; a procedure invented for safety-relevant hardware would be worse than none.

methods.description: Physical access to the CAN harness via a D-Sub 9 breakout and a SocketCAN-compatible interface at 500 kbit/s. There is no onboarding handshake for a third-party client -- the bus is simply there.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision. Nothing a third party can provision. Component pairing exists but is gated behind Bosch dealer tooling, which is precisely the dependency this target documents.

rejoin.notes: No network binding exists, so there is nothing to rejoin. Moving the vehicle between owners or workshops changes nothing about how the bus is reached.

testing.notes: CAN-layer facts checked against a first-party candump of a real ride (research store: bosch-ebike-cx-gen4/captures/candump-tour-001.log). The BLE surface is static-analysis only; nothing has been driven end-to-end from this spec by this project.

services.notes: 128-bit vendor UUID declared alongside the MCSP/BSS UUIDs in the app's BLE manager. The inspected code paths do not reveal its role; listed so nobody has to guess. App-confirmed UUID, purpose unknown, not hardware-tested.

characteristics.name: Meta
characteristics.notes: UUID spells "BOSCH MCSP  Meta". 3-byte value: protocol version byte + 16-bit big-endian max payload; the app requests ATT MTU 253 when the meta version is > 1, else keeps 23 App-confirmed, not hardware-tested.

characteristics.name: MISO
characteristics.notes: UUID spells "BOSCH MCSP  MISO". Display-to-app data; the app enables notifications on it. Carries SimpleTransportMessage fragments. App-confirmed, not hardware-tested.

characteristics.name: MOSI
characteristics.notes: UUID spells "BOSCH MCSP  MOSI". App-to-display direction inferred from the MOSI naming and the CoAP request flow; the exact write call site was not pinned down in the app's code. App-confirmed, not hardware-tested.

services.name: BOSCH MCSP v1
services.notes:
Data channel of the Kiox BLE link; the UUID's first ten bytes spell "BOSCH MCSP" in ASCII, followed by 'v' and the binary version bytes 01 00 00 (v1.0.0) — not the literal text "v1". Carries CoAP requests/responses with protobuf bodies inside an encrypted, fragmented transport (app-confirmed, not hardware-tested):
FRAMING (bottom up). BLE writes/notifications carry SimpleTransport- Message fragments: a 2-byte header -- byte 0 = version (2 bits, only 0 accepted) | firstPart (bit 5) | lastPart (bit 4) | counter (low nibble, 0..15), byte 1 = payload length 0..255; reassembly checks first/last flags and counter order mod 16. Reassembled bytes form a SimpleMessage: 4-byte header -- byte 0 = version (2 bits) | domain (6 bits), byte 1 = message type, bytes 2-3 = payload length big-endian -- then payload, then a 2-byte big-endian CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE trailer (init 0xFFFF, poly 0x1021, MSB-first, no reflection, no final XOR) over header+payload.
SECURITY. Before data flows, key establishment runs over the BSS service below (message domain KEY_ESTABLISHMENT): certificate-based Diffie-Hellman -- KeyExchangeStep1Request carries entity / device_certificate / dh_public_b / signature, the step-2 response carries chacha_encrypted / chacha_mac / ble_key (protobuf descriptors ship in the app's key-establishment package), with session keys expanded via HKDF. Afterwards every message is ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD: 20-round ChaCha, 12-byte nonce, 16-byte Poly1305 tag, AAD = 8-byte little-endian message counter || length, with per-direction rolling counters and replay rejection on counter mismatch.
ENDPOINTS. CoAP paths observed in the app: v1/battery, v1/activity, v1/firmware, v1/available_firmware, v1/echo, v1/version, v1/user, v1/timezone, v1/timestamp, v1/system_description, v1/location, v1/location_subscribe, v1/notification, v1/backend_token, v1/saved_route_list, v1/saved_route_details, v1/saved_destinations, v1/udams, v1/licenses, v1/a_gnss_offline, v1/a_gnss_online, v1/weather, v1/instant_route, v1/disabler_service. DRIVE-UNIT LOCK/UNLOCK: the "Lock" feature talks to v1/disabler_service with a DisablerServiceBuiRequest protobuf (SEND_KEY etc.), backed by backend REST calls (postLockService/postUnlockService).

characteristics.name: MISO
characteristics.notes: UUID spells "BOSCH BSS  MISO". Display-to-app; the app enables indications, falling back to notifications if the indicate property is absent. App-confirmed, not hardware-tested.

characteristics.name: MOSI
characteristics.notes: UUID spells "BOSCH BSS  MOSI". App-to-display direction inferred from the MOSI naming and the handshake flow; the exact write call site was not pinned down in the app's code. App-confirmed, not hardware-tested.

services.name: BOSCH BSS v1
services.notes: Security channel of the Kiox BLE link; the UUID's first ten bytes spell "BOSCH BSSv" in ASCII, followed by 'v' and the binary version bytes 01 00 00 (v1.0.0) — not the literal text "v1". Carries the key-establishment handshake described under the MCSP service (SimpleMessage domain KEY_ESTABLISHMENT), in the same fragmented/CRC'd transport. Pairing is backend-gated: it needs the per-device encryptedPreSharedKey provisioned from the Bosch backend (app-confirmed on the device record and the connect path). Not hardware-tested.
